lessons.title: Plan a goodbye party for a teacher
lessons.goal: I can plan a goodbye party and invite people to it.

newItems.definition: A warm way to say hello or goodbye with your arms.
newItems.example: We will give Ms. Reed a big hug.

newItems.definition: Funny in a happy and not serious way.
newItems.example: We can play a silly game at the party.

newItems.definition: A friendly way to ask people to come to a party or a game.
newItems.example: Come and join us at the party.

newItems.definition: A party to say goodbye to a person who is leaving.
newItems.example: We plan a goodbye party for Ms. Reed.

newItems.definition: A way to ask someone to look at something.
newItems.example: Take a look at our plan for the party.

mainWord.definition: A warm way to say hello or goodbye with your arms.
mainWord.example: We will give Ms. Reed a big hug.

lessons.mainWordForms: Hug is a verb. The past is hugged. A hug is a warm way to say hello or goodbye with your arms.
lessons.expression: Come and join us at the goodbye party.
lessons.use: Plan a goodbye party and invite people to it.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Noah about the goodbye party. Invite him to join us.
lessons.grammar: Come and join us at + noun
lessons.pattern: Come and join us at + noun
lessons.task: Come and join us ___ the party.
lessons.example: Come and join us at the party.
context: Ms. Reed is leaving our school next week. The class wants to plan a goodbye party for her.
Come and join us at the goodbye party. Take a look at our plan for Friday.
dialogue: Ms. Reed is leaving our school next week. Let us plan a goodbye party for her.
Good idea. Come and join us at the party on Friday. We can sing songs.
Yes. We can play a silly game too. What food do we need?
Let us take a look at our plan. We need a cake and drinks.
I will bring a cake. Can you bring the drinks?
Yes. At the party, we will give Ms. Reed a hug and say thank you.
lessons.listening: Ms. Reed is leaving our school next week. Mia and Noah plan a goodbye party for her. They will sing songs and play a silly game. Come and join us at the party. They will give Ms. Reed a hug and say thank you.
lessons.question: When is the goodbye party?
lessons.reading: Ms. Reed is leaving our school next week. Her class wants to plan a goodbye party for her. Mia says, “Come and join us at the party. We can sing songs and play a silly game.” Noah says, “Good idea. Let us take a look at our plan. We need food and drinks.” Mia smiles and says, “Yes. I will bring a cake. You can bring drinks.” Noah says, “Good. At the party, we will give Ms. Reed a hug and say thank you. She is a good teacher, and we will miss her.”
lessons.readingQ: What will they give Ms. Reed at the party?
lessons.speaking: Plan a goodbye party with a partner. Say who the party is for, say what you will do, and invite your partner to join.
lessons.speakingSample: We want to plan a goodbye party for Ms. Reed. Come and join us at the party on Friday. We can sing songs and play a silly game. Let us take a look at our plan. We will give Ms. Reed a hug and say thank you.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a goodbye party for a teacher. Say who the party is for, say what you will do, and invite people to join.
lessons.writingSample: Ms. Reed is leaving our school next week. Her class wants to plan a goodbye party for her. Mia says, “Come and join us at the party. We can sing songs and play a silly game.” Noah says, “Good idea. Let us take a look at our plan.” At the party, we will give Ms. Reed a hug and say thank you.
lessons.sound: Hug has its strongest beat on HUG. In silly, say SIL clearly. In take a look, say LOOK clearly at the end.
lessons.model: Come and join us at the party. We will give Ms. Reed a hug.
lessons.wordSample: We will give Ms. Reed a big hug.
lessons.wordTask: What will the class give Ms. Reed?

lessons.title: Ask about a swimming class on the phone
lessons.goal: I can ask for information about a class on the phone.

newItems.definition: Not afraid of something new or difficult.
newItems.example: Be brave and try the swimming class.

newItems.definition: A small room where you change your clothes.
newItems.example: You can change in the changing room.

newItems.definition: A way to say the price for one month.
newItems.example: The class costs ten dollars per month.

newItems.definition: A way to tell someone to be quick.
newItems.example: Hurry up, Leo. The class starts at four.

newItems.definition: A way to say you do something alone, with no other people.
newItems.example: I go to the class by myself.

mainWord.definition: Not afraid of something new or difficult.
mainWord.example: Be brave and try the swimming class.

lessons.mainWordForms: Brave is an adjective. A brave person is not afraid of something new. Be brave and try the class.
lessons.expression: I go to the class by myself.
lessons.use: Ask for information about a class on the phone.
lessons.expressionTask: Phone the sports centre. Ask about the class and say you go by yourself.
lessons.pattern: It costs ten dollars per month
lessons.task: The class costs ten dollars ___ month.
lessons.example: The class costs ten dollars per month.
context: Leo phones the sports centre to ask about a swimming class for children.
I go to the class by myself. The class costs ten dollars per month.

photo.caption: Children learn to swim with their coach in an outdoor pool.
photo.alt: Children learning to swim with a coach in an outdoor pool.

dialogue: Hurry up, Leo. Phone the sports centre now.
Hello. I want to join a swimming class. How much does it cost?
It costs ten dollars per month. How old are you?
I am nine years old. Where can I change my clothes?
You can change in the changing room. Be brave and try the class.
Thank you. I will come on Monday. I go to the class by myself.
lessons.listening: Leo phones the sports centre to ask about a swimming class. It costs ten dollars per month. He can change in the changing room. Leo is brave and he will try the class. Mum says, “Hurry up, Leo. The class starts at four.”
lessons.question: How much does the swimming class cost?
lessons.reading: Leo phones the sports centre to ask about a swimming class for children. A man says, “Hello. How can I help you?” Leo says, “I want to join a swimming class. How much does it cost?” The man says, “It costs ten dollars per month. You can change in the changing room. Be brave and try the class.” Leo smiles and says, “Good. I go to the class by myself. Mum says, ‘Hurry up, Leo. The class starts at four.’” Leo says, “Thank you. I am happy. I will see you on Monday.”
lessons.readingQ: Where can Leo change his clothes?
lessons.speaking: Ask about a swimming class on the phone with a partner. Ask the price, ask where to change, and say you will go by yourself.
lessons.speakingSample: I want to join a swimming class. How much does it cost? It costs ten dollars per month. You can change in the changing room. Be brave and try the class. I go to the class by myself. Mum says, “Hurry up, Leo. The class starts at four.”
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a phone call to a sports centre. Ask about a swimming class, ask the price, and say you will go by yourself.
lessons.writingSample: Leo phones the sports centre to ask about a swimming class for children. He says, “I want to join a swimming class. How much does it cost?” The man says, “It costs ten dollars per month. You can change in the changing room. Be brave and try the class.” Leo says, “Good. I go to the class by myself.”
lessons.sound: Brave has its strongest beat on BRAVE. In changing room, say CHANG clearly. In per month, say MONTH clearly at the end.
lessons.model: Be brave and try the class. You can change in the changing room.
lessons.wordSample: Be brave and try the class.

lessons.title: Choose a holiday: mountains or seaside
lessons.goal: I can choose a holiday and say why I prefer it.

newItems.definition: Not wide; a narrow road is small from side to side.
newItems.example: The path to the lake is narrow.

newItems.definition: Very quiet, with no sound.
newItems.example: The lake is silent in the morning.

newItems.definition: Not usual; something you do not know or do not expect.
newItems.example: There is a strange old house near the lake.

newItems.definition: Quiet with new people; a shy person does not talk a lot.
newItems.example: I am a little shy, but I like to meet new people.

newItems.definition: A polite way to say you like one thing more than another.
newItems.example: I'd prefer the mountains.

mainWord.definition: Not wide; a narrow road is small from side to side.
mainWord.example: The path to the lake is narrow.

lessons.mainWordForms: Narrow is an adjective. A narrow road is not wide. The path to the lake is narrow.
lessons.use: Choose a holiday and say why you prefer it.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Noah about the holiday. Say you prefer the mountains.
context: Mia and Noah plan a holiday. They can go to the mountains or to the seaside.
I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent, and the path is narrow.

photo.caption: A calm lake lies silent in the morning between misty mountains.
photo.alt: A still mountain lake surrounded by misty mountains.

dialogue: We can go to the mountains or to the seaside. Which holiday do you like?
I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent in the morning.
Yes, but the path is narrow. Is it a good place for us?
Yes. There is a strange old house near the lake. We can see it.
I am a little shy, but I like to meet new people on holiday.
Good. Let us go to the mountains on Saturday.
lessons.listening: Mia and Noah plan a holiday. They can go to the mountains or to the seaside. Mia says, “I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent, and the path is narrow.” Noah likes the seaside, but Mia likes the mountains. They will go on Saturday.
lessons.question: What does Mia prefer?
lessons.reading: Mia and Noah plan a holiday. They can go to the mountains or to the seaside. Mia says, “I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent in the morning, and the path is narrow.” Noah says, “I like the seaside. But the mountains are good too. Is there a strange old house near the lake?” Mia says, “Yes. It is very old, but it is a good place to see. I am a little shy, but I like to meet new people.” Noah says, “Good. Let us go to the mountains on Saturday.”
lessons.speaking: Choose a holiday with a partner. Say the two places, say what you prefer, and say why.
lessons.speakingSample: We plan a holiday. We can go to the mountains or to the seaside. I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent in the morning, and the path is narrow. There is a strange old house near the lake. I am shy, but I like to meet new people.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a holiday choice. Say the two places, say what you prefer, and say why.
lessons.writingSample: Mia and Noah plan a holiday. They can go to the mountains or to the seaside. Mia says, “I'd prefer the mountains. The lake is silent in the morning, and the path is narrow.” Noah says, “I like the seaside.” Mia says, “There is a strange old house near the lake. I am a little shy, but I like to meet new people.”
lessons.sound: Narrow has its strongest beat on NAR. In silent, say SI clearly. In I'd prefer, say FER clearly at the end.
lessons.model: The path is narrow and silent. I'd prefer the mountains.
lessons.wordSample: The path to the lake is narrow.

lessons.title: Start a community garden
lessons.goal: I can plan a community garden and say what we will do.

newItems.definition: A small thing you put in the ground; a plant grows from it.
newItems.example: Put the seed in the ground.

newItems.definition: To put a seed in the ground so it can grow.
newItems.example: We plant seeds in the spring.

newItems.definition: To make a hole in the ground with your hands or a tool.
newItems.example: I can dig the ground on Saturday.

newItems.definition: A way to say you make vegetables grow in a garden.
newItems.example: We can grow vegetables here.

newItems.definition: A way to say you give water to plants so they can grow.
newItems.example: We plant seeds and water the plants every week.

mainWord.definition: A small thing you put in the ground; a plant grows from it.
mainWord.example: Put the seed in the ground.

lessons.mainWordForms: Seed is a noun. The plural is seeds. A seed is small, and a plant grows from a seed.
lessons.use: Plan a community garden and say what we will do.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Ana about the garden. Say you can grow vegetables here.
lessons.pattern: We can grow vegetables in the garden
lessons.task: We can grow ___ in the garden.
lessons.example: We can grow vegetables in the garden.
context: Mia, Noah, Leo and Ana want to start a garden on their street.
We can grow vegetables here. We plant seeds and water the plants every week.

photo.caption: Children and an adult garden together in a lush green garden.
photo.alt: Children and an adult gardening together in a green garden.

dialogue: We want to start a garden on our street. What can we grow?
We can grow vegetables here. We plant seeds and water the plants every week.
Good idea. I can dig the ground on Saturday. What seeds do we need?
We need seeds for carrots and beans. Can you bring them?
Yes. I will bring the seeds on Saturday morning.
Good. Our garden will be very good for our street.
lessons.listening: Mia, Noah, Leo and Ana want to start a garden on their street. They can grow vegetables there. They plant seeds and water the plants every week. Noah can dig the ground on Saturday. Ana will bring seeds for carrots and beans.
lessons.question: What will Noah do on Saturday?
lessons.reading: Mia, Noah, Leo and Ana want to start a garden on their street. The garden is near their school. Mia says, “We can grow vegetables here. We plant seeds and water the plants every week.” Noah says, “Good idea. I can dig the ground on Saturday. We need seeds and water.” Ana says, “I will bring seeds for carrots and beans. We can grow vegetables for our families.” Leo says, “Yes. We plant seeds in the spring, and we water the plants every week. Our garden will be very good for our street.”
lessons.readingQ: What can they grow in the garden?
lessons.speaking: Plan a garden with a partner. Say what you will grow, say who will dig, and say what you need.
lessons.speakingSample: We want to start a garden on our street. We can grow vegetables here. We plant seeds and water the plants every week. I can dig the ground on Saturday. Ana will bring seeds for carrots and beans. Our garden will be very good for our street.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a garden on your street. Say what you will grow, say who will dig, and say what you need.
lessons.writingSample: Mia, Noah, Leo and Ana want to start a garden on their street. Mia says, “We can grow vegetables here. We plant seeds and water the plants every week.” Noah says, “Good idea. I can dig the ground on Saturday. We need seeds and water.” Ana will bring seeds for carrots and beans. Our garden will be very good for our street.
lessons.sound: Seed has its strongest beat on SEED. In plant, say PLANT clearly. In water the plants, say PLANTS clearly at the end.
lessons.model: Put the seed in the ground. We plant seeds and water the plants.
lessons.wordSample: Put the seed in the ground.
lessons.wordTask: Where do we put the seed?

lessons.title: Tell the story of a day at the zoo
lessons.goal: I can tell the story of a day at the zoo and aquarium.

newItems.definition: A black and white bird that cannot fly but can swim.
newItems.example: We saw a penguin at the zoo.

newItems.definition: A bird that sleeps in the day and is awake at night.
newItems.example: The owl sleeps in the day.

newItems.definition: A big bird with a strong beak that flies very high.
newItems.example: We also saw an eagle.

newItems.definition: A very big animal that lives in the sea.
newItems.example: We saw a whale and a dolphin.

newItems.definition: A clever sea animal that can swim and jump very well.
newItems.example: We saw a whale and a dolphin.

mainWord.definition: A black and white bird that cannot fly but can swim.
mainWord.example: We saw a penguin at the zoo.

lessons.mainWordForms: Penguin is a noun. The plural is penguins. A penguin is a black and white bird. It cannot fly, but it can swim.
lessons.expression: We saw a whale and a dolphin.
lessons.use: Tell the story of a day at the zoo and aquarium.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Leo about the zoo. Say you saw a whale and a dolphin.
lessons.pattern: We saw a whale at the aquarium
lessons.task: We saw a ___ at the aquarium.
lessons.example: We saw a whale at the aquarium.
context: Ana tells the story of a day at the zoo and the aquarium with her family.
We saw a whale and a dolphin. The penguin is funny and the owl is quiet.

photo.caption: A Gentoo penguin stands in its habitat at the zoo.
photo.alt: A Gentoo penguin standing in a zoo habitat.

dialogue: Ana, tell us the story of your day at the zoo.
In the morning, we saw a penguin and an owl. The penguin is very funny.
What does the owl do in the day?
The owl sleeps in the day. It is a quiet bird.
What did you see in the afternoon?
We saw a whale and a dolphin at the aquarium. We also saw an eagle.
lessons.listening: Ana tells the story of a day at the zoo. In the morning, she saw a penguin and an owl. In the afternoon, she saw a whale and a dolphin at the aquarium. The whale is very big. She also saw an eagle.
lessons.question: What did Ana see in the afternoon?
lessons.reading: Ana tells the story of a day at the zoo and the aquarium with her family. She says, “In the morning, we saw a penguin and an owl. The penguin is very funny, and the owl sleeps in the day.” Ana says, “In the afternoon, we went to the aquarium. We saw a whale and a dolphin. The whale is very big, and the dolphin is very quick.” Ana smiles and says, “We also saw an eagle. The eagle is a big bird with a strong beak. It was a very good day.”
lessons.speaking: Tell the story of a day at the zoo with a partner. Say what you saw in the morning and in the afternoon.
lessons.speakingSample: We went to the zoo and the aquarium. In the morning, we saw a penguin and an owl. The penguin is very funny, and the owl sleeps in the day. In the afternoon, we saw a whale and a dolphin. The whale is very big. We also saw an eagle.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a day at the zoo. Say what you saw in the morning and in the afternoon.
lessons.writingSample: Ana tells the story of a day at the zoo and the aquarium with her family. In the morning, they saw a penguin and an owl. The penguin is very funny, and the owl sleeps in the day. In the afternoon, they saw a whale and a dolphin. The whale is very big. They also saw an eagle.
lessons.sound: Penguin has its strongest beat on PEN. In owl, say OWL clearly. In dolphin, say DOL clearly at the start.
lessons.model: The penguin is funny. The owl sleeps in the day.
lessons.wordSample: We saw a penguin at the zoo.
lessons.wordTask: What did they see at the zoo?

lessons.title: Tell a story about an old castle
lessons.goal: I can tell a story about an old castle.

newItems.definition: A tall part of a castle; you can see far from the top.
newItems.example: The castle has a very tall tower.

newItems.definition: Gold and jewels that people keep in a secret place.
newItems.example: In the room, there is a box with a treasure.

newItems.definition: Something that only some people know.
newItems.example: There is a secret room in the tower.

newItems.definition: A special power that can do strange and wonderful things.
newItems.example: The magic key opens the door.

newItems.definition: A white shape of a dead person that some people see at night.
newItems.example: A ghost lives in the castle.

mainWord.definition: A tall part of a castle; you can see far from the top.
mainWord.example: The castle has a very tall tower.

lessons.mainWordForms: Tower is a noun. The plural is towers. A tower is a tall part of a castle. You can see far from the top of a tower.
lessons.expression: There is a secret room in the tower.
lessons.use: Tell a story about an old castle.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Mia about the castle. Say there is a secret room in the tower.
lessons.grammar: There is a + noun + in the tower
lessons.pattern: There is a secret room in the tower
lessons.task: There is a secret ___ in the tower.
lessons.example: There is a secret room in the tower.
context: Leo tells a story about an old castle on a hill.
There is a secret room in the tower. The magic key opens the door.

photo.caption: An old medieval castle stands on a forested hill under a cloudy sky.
photo.alt: A medieval castle on a forested hill under a cloudy sky.

dialogue: Leo, tell us a story about the old castle.
The castle has a very tall tower. There is a secret room in the tower.
What opens the door to the room?
The magic key opens the door. In the room, there is a box with a treasure.
Is there a ghost in the castle?
Yes. A ghost lives in the castle. At night, the ghost sings a song.
lessons.listening: Leo tells a story about an old castle. The castle has a very tall tower. There is a secret room in the tower. The magic key opens the door. In the room, there is a box with a treasure. A ghost lives in the castle.
lessons.question: What is in the room?
lessons.reading: Leo tells a story about an old castle on a hill. He says, “The castle has a very tall tower. There is a secret room in the tower. The magic key opens the door.” Leo says, “In the room, there is a box with a treasure. The treasure is gold and red jewels. But a ghost lives in the castle. The ghost is white and very quiet.” Leo smiles and says, “At night, the ghost sings a song. The children are not afraid. It is a funny ghost. The children like the story.”
lessons.speaking: Tell a story about an old castle with a partner. Say what is in the tower and what is in the room.
lessons.speakingSample: Leo tells a story about an old castle. The castle has a very tall tower. There is a secret room in the tower. The magic key opens the door. In the room, there is a box with a treasure. But a ghost lives in the castle.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about an old castle. Say what is in the tower and what is in the room.
lessons.writingSample: Leo tells a story about an old castle on a hill. The castle has a very tall tower. There is a secret room in the tower. The magic key opens the door. In the room, there is a box with a treasure. The treasure is gold and red jewels. But a ghost lives in the castle. The ghost is white and very quiet.
lessons.sound: Tower has its strongest beat on TOW. In treasure, say TREAS clearly. In secret, say SE clearly at the start.
lessons.model: The tower is very old. There is a secret room in the tower.
lessons.wordSample: The castle has a very tall tower.

lessons.title: Spend a day at the museum
lessons.goal: I can talk about a day at the museum and ask for help.

newItems.definition: A place with old and interesting things to look at and learn about.
newItems.example: It is a very famous museum.

newItems.definition: Known by many people; a famous place is one many people know.
newItems.example: It is a very famous museum.

newItems.definition: A way to add a new idea when you are talking.
newItems.example: By the way, the museum is open on Sunday.

newItems.definition: A friendly way to tell someone not to be afraid or sad.
newItems.example: Don't worry, it will be all right.

newItems.definition: A way to say that a problem will be fine in the end.
newItems.example: Don't worry, it will be all right.

mainWord.definition: A place with old and interesting things to look at and learn about.
mainWord.example: It is a very famous museum.

lessons.mainWordForms: Museum is a noun. The plural is museums. A museum is a place with old and interesting things. You can look and learn in a museum.
lessons.expression: Don't worry, it will be all right.
lessons.use: Talk about a day at the museum and ask for help.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Noah about the rain. Say not to worry, it will be all right.
lessons.pattern: Don't worry, it will be all right
lessons.task: Don't worry, it will be ___ right.
lessons.example: Don't worry, it will be all right.
context: Mia and Noah spend a day at the museum in the city. Mia is worried about the rain.
Don't worry, it will be all right. By the way, the museum is open on Sunday.

photo.caption: Visitors walk through a grand museum hall under a high arched ceiling.
photo.alt: Visitors in a grand museum hall with statues.

dialogue: We spend a day at the museum in the city. Are you worried about the rain?
Yes. I am worried. What can we do?
Don't worry, it will be all right. By the way, the museum is open on Sunday.
Good. I like the museum. Can we see the old trains?
Yes. The museum has old trains, old cars and old boats.
It is a very famous museum. I am happy to be here.
lessons.listening: Mia and Noah spend a day at the museum in the city. It is a very famous museum. Mia is worried about the rain. Noah says, “Don't worry, it will be all right.” They see old trains and old cars there.
lessons.question: What is Mia worried about?
lessons.reading: Mia and Noah spend a day at the museum in the city. They go there by train in the morning. It is a very famous museum with old and interesting things. Mia is worried about the rain. Noah says, “Don't worry, it will be all right. By the way, the museum is open on Sunday.” Mia smiles and says, “Good. I like the museum. By the way, can we see the old trains?” Noah says, “Yes. The museum has old trains, old cars and old boats. It is a very good day.”
lessons.readingA: Old trains, old cars and old boats.
lessons.speaking: Talk about a day at the museum with a partner. Say how you go there, say what you see, and say not to worry.
lessons.speakingSample: We spend a day at the museum in the city. We go there by train in the morning. It is a very famous museum. Don't worry, it will be all right. By the way, the museum is open on Sunday. We can see old trains and old cars.
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about a day at the museum. Say how you go there, say what you see, and say not to worry.
lessons.writingSample: Mia and Noah spend a day at the museum in the city. They go there by train in the morning. It is a famous museum with old and interesting things. Mia is worried about the rain. Noah says, “Don't worry, it will be all right. By the way, the museum is open on Sunday.” The museum has old trains, old cars and old boats.
lessons.sound: Museum has its strongest beat on SE. In famous, say FAM clearly. In by the way, say WAY clearly at the end.
lessons.model: The museum is famous. By the way, it is open on Sunday.
lessons.wordSample: It is a very famous museum.

lessons.title: Welcome new neighbours
lessons.goal: I can welcome new neighbours and help them settle in.

newItems.definition: To start to feel at home in a new place.
newItems.example: We can help them settle in.

newItems.definition: A way to say you help new people feel at home.
newItems.example: We can help them settle in.

newItems.definition: A way to say you say hello to the people near your home for the first time.
newItems.example: Let us meet the neighbours at a welcome picnic.

newItems.definition: A way to say a person has just come to live in a town.
newItems.example: A new family, the Browns, is new in town.

newItems.definition: A picnic to say hello to new people in a friendly way.
newItems.example: Let us meet the neighbours at a welcome picnic.

mainWord.definition: To start to feel at home in a new place.
mainWord.example: We can help them settle in.

lessons.mainWordForms: Settle is a verb. The past is settled. To settle in means to feel at home in a new place. A new family needs time to settle in.
lessons.expression: We can help them settle in.
lessons.use: Welcome new neighbours and help them settle in.
lessons.expressionTask: Tell Ben about the Browns. Say you can help them settle in.
lessons.pattern: We can help them settle in
lessons.example: We can help them settle in.
context: A new family, the Browns, is new in town. Emma and Ben want to welcome them.
We can help them settle in. Let us meet the neighbours at a welcome picnic.
dialogue: A new family, the Browns, is new in town. How can we welcome them?
We can help them settle in. Let us meet the neighbours at a welcome picnic.
Good idea. We can have the picnic in the park on Saturday.
Yes. I will bring food and drinks. What will you bring?
I will bring a cake. We can show them our street.
Good. The Browns will be very happy. A welcome picnic is a good way to meet new people.
lessons.listening: A new family, the Browns, is new in town. Emma and Ben want to welcome them. They can help them settle in. They will meet the neighbours at a welcome picnic in the park on Saturday. Ben will bring food and drinks.
lessons.question: Where is the welcome picnic?
lessons.reading: A new family, the Browns, is new in town. Emma and Ben want to welcome them. Emma says, “We can help them settle in.
